land.text: Medina and the Hejaz, then Arabia re-united in the Ridda wars (633)

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: First Islamic state'. The Medina state is a dossier written by this group.

land.text: the whole caliphate, to which Mu'awiya succeeded in 661

successors.note: Syria and Egypt were already Mu'awiya's from 656 and 658.

capitals.name: Medina
capitals.note: Infobox: Medina (632-656); Uthman was killed there in June 656.

rulers.name: Hasan ibn Ali
rulers.note: Six months in 661, before his abdication (First Fitna page; infobox '661: Hasan ibn Ali').

correction.text: 632: Medina and the Hejaz; the rest of Arabia in revolt until March 633

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 633. In 632 the page gives only Medina as the capital and the Ridda wars still to fight; the peninsula was 'united under the caliph in Medina' only by 18 March 633. The Hejaz is the reading of 'Medina', not a boundary the page draws.

2.54 M km2, Arabia (91% of the region) with Yemen and Oman: matches 'The Arabian Peninsula ... united under the caliph in Medina' by 18 March 633. Hira (May 633, 100 km, tributary) is below the resolution of this shape and is carried by the 634 shape.

3.2 M km2 for 634-637: Arabia, about half of the Levant and about 40% of Mesopotamia. Damascus 634 or 635, the Yarmuk (August 636), Jerusalem (April 637), Ctesiphon (March 637) and Antioch (October 637) all fall inside the span; the ledger gives the steps and the soft frontier is right to within a year or two.

3.77 M km2: the Levant, the Jazira (Raqqa 639-640, Upper Mesopotamia) and Mesopotamia, with Byzantine Armenia (638-639). Khuzestan is not inside the shape, correctly: Hormuzan is a tributary from late 638 (ledger vassal), Susa falls in January 641.

correction.text: 641: the 641 shape plus Khuzestan (Susa, January 641); the Median plateau, Isfahan and Kerman follow in 642 and 643 (the next two keyframes)

keyframe_review.note: 4.40 M km2 for 641-643 adds Egypt (642) but has almost nothing in Iran (1%). Susa fell in January 641 and Nahavand in December 642, so Khuzestan belongs inside from 641. Applies to 641 only; the Hamadan and Rey events of December 642 and the Isfahan, Kerman, Cyrenaica and Tripolitania events of 643 have their own keyframes (review of 2026-10-19).

correction.text: 642: the 641 shape plus Khuzestan, Hamadan and Rey

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Nahavand (December 642) and the district of Hamadan; Rey is carried at confidence 1 in step with the Sasanian loss of Media in 642.

correction.text: 643: plus Isfahan, Kerman, Cyrenaica and Tripolitania

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kerman subdued in 643, Isfahan carried at 643 (confidence 1), and Amr's advance into Cyrenaica and Tripolitania, with Tripoli 'around 643' (Maghreb page). Cliopatria's shapes have no Libya before 647.

correction.text: 644: the 644 shape minus Khorasan, Sistan, Afghanistan, Tabaristan, the Pakistani land outside Makran and Fars, plus Cyrenaica and Tripolitania

keyframe_review.note: 6.74 M km2 for 644-646 gives the caliphate all of Iran, Khorasan, Sistan and Afghanistan, but Sistan and Khorasan fell only in 651 and 'Tabaristan and Transoxiana remained outside Muslim domination'. Fars is held back until Istakhr surrenders in 648 (review of 2026-10-19), and of the 208,000 km2 of Pakistan in the shape only Makran (155,000 km2) is kept, because the Makran page ends the conquest there ('the easternmost frontier'). Applies to 644; 645 and 646 follow.
New keyframe: the Byzantine fleet takes Alexandria at the end of 645 (Egypt page); a 60 km radius, drawn for completeness.
New keyframe: Alexandria is retaken in 646. Armenia and Azerbaijan, which rebel in 646, stay in the shape while contested (ledger: contest pairs to 651 and 653).

correction.text: 647: the 647 shape minus Khorasan, Sistan, Afghanistan, Tabaristan, the Pakistani land outside Makran, Fars and Ifriqiya, plus Cyrenaica and Tripolitania

keyframe_review.note: 7.09 M km2 for 647-655; the infobox gives 6.4 M km2 for 655 (ratio 0.90, fine). The shape has Khorasan, Sistan and Afghanistan from 647 (fallen 651), Ifriqiya at 13% (Sufetula was a raid; the army withdrew to Barqa) and no Cyprus (649). Ifriqiya includes Tripolitania, which is added back (Tripoli 643). Applies to 647; 648, 649-650, 651-652 and 653-655 follow.
New keyframe: 'In 648 ... forced the governor of Estakhr, Mahak, to surrender the city'; the Fars revolt of 649-651 is a contest pair in the ledger.
New keyframe: Cyprus taken by Mu'awiya's fleet in 649 (Levant page), 650 on the Rashidun page.

correction.text: 651-652: the 647 shape minus Ifriqiya and the Pakistani land outside Makran, plus Cyrenaica, Tripolitania and Cyprus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 651-652 after Khorasan and Sistan (651) and the reconquest of Azerbaijan, Hamadan and Rey. 'Tabaristan and Transoxiana remained outside' (peace treaty 651); Afghanistan beyond Khorasan and Sistan (about 190,000 km2) stays in the shape as Cliopatria draws it, with no gain event: the pages opened are silent (gap). Infobox 6.4 M km2 for 655.

minus.text: 653-655: as 651-652, without Armenia, which submits as a tributary
Armenia, the principality's outline (principality-of-armenia keyframes 644-884), including the 36 cells outside the Armenian Highlands region

correction.text: 653-655: as 651-652, without Armenia, which submits as a tributary; without the principality of Armenia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Armenia becomes a tributary under Theodore Rshtuni in 653 (Armenia page) and is drawn as a vassal, outside the shape, to 657. Infobox 6.4 M km2 for 655. As resolved this keyframe covers about 6.9 M km2 against the infobox's 6.4 M km2 for 655 (ratio 0.93, within the factor of two); Cyrenaica and Tripolitania are drawn as the 692 Umayyad shape has them (360,000 km2), not as the whole gazetteer regions. Repair fx-01 (conflict with principality-of-armenia, 945 cell-years; hierarchy fix F183): 653-655: Rshtuni 'voluntarily agreed to submit to Muslim overlordship' (a tributary, drawn outside the shape). The region 'Armenian Highlands' already subtracted here covers only 147 of the principality's 183 cells, and the 661 shape put all 183 back, so the compiler gave the cells to the principality by the size rule at 658 and 661; the principality's own outline is now subtracted. Muslim conquest of Armenia page.

minus.text: Ali's caliphate without Syria and Cyprus, Egypt still inside, for 656-657: the Cliopatria shape minus Armenia, Ifriqiya and the Pakistani land outside Makran, plus Cyrenaica and Tripolitania
Armenia, the principality's outline (principality-of-armenia keyframes 644-884), including the 36 cells outside the Armenian Highlands region

correction.text: Ali's caliphate without Syria and Cyprus, Egypt still inside, for 656-657: the Cliopatria shape minus Armenia, Ifriqiya and the Pakistani land outside Makran, plus Cyrenaica and Tripolitania; without the principality of Armenia

keyframe_review.note: 6.52 M km2 for 656-660 without Syria (Mu'awiya's) but with Egypt, which Mu'awiya annexed in 658; and without Cyprus, which went with Syria. Right for 656-657 once Armenia (a Byzantine overlordship from 657) and the Ifriqiya remnant are taken out. Libya is kept to 661: no page opened says which side held it in 658-660. Repair fx-01 (conflict with principality-of-armenia, 945 cell-years; hierarchy fix F183): 656-657: Armenia is a tributary until 'with the outbreak of the First Muslim Civil War in 657, effective Arab authority in the country ceased'. The region 'Armenian Highlands' already subtracted here covers only 147 of the principality's 183 cells, and the 661 shape put all 183 back, so the compiler gave the cells to the principality by the size rule at 658 and 661; the principality's own outline is now subtracted. Muslim conquest of Armenia page.

minus.text: Armenia, the principality's outline (principality-of-armenia keyframes 644-884), including the 36 cells outside the Armenian Highlands region

correction.text: 658-660: the 656 correction minus Egypt; without the principality of Armenia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 658 'Mu'awiya held Syria and, from 658, Egypt'; Ali held Iraq and, until Busr's raids in 660, the Hejaz and Yemen. Repair fx-01 (conflict with principality-of-armenia, 945 cell-years; hierarchy fix F183): 658-660: 'Mamikonian returned to Byzantine overlordship almost immediately' after 657. The region 'Armenian Highlands' already subtracted here covers only 147 of the principality's 183 cells, and the 661 shape put all 183 back, so the compiler gave the cells to the principality by the size rule at 658 and 661; the principality's own outline is now subtracted. Muslim conquest of Armenia page.

minus.text: 661 only, to Hasan's abdication: the shape unchanged; 662-665 belongs to the Umayyad Caliphate
Armenia, the principality's outline (principality-of-armenia keyframes 644-884), including the 36 cells outside the Armenian Highlands region

correction.text: 661 only, to Hasan's abdication: the shape unchanged; 662-665 belongs to the Umayyad Caliphate; without the principality of Armenia

keyframe_review.note: 5.87 M km2 for 661-665 keeps Arabia, Iraq and Iran under the Rashidun name for five years. Ali was killed in January 661 and Hasan abdicated after six months; the land is Umayyad from 661 (Umayyad dossier, which merges it in its 661 keyframe). The shape is right for 661 alone. Repair fx-01 (conflict with principality-of-armenia, 945 cell-years; hierarchy fix F183): 661: Armenia returns to the caliph only when 'Mu'awiya ... ordered the Armenian princes to re-submit to his authority and pay tribute' (Umayyad, after Ali's death); until then it is under Byzantine overlordship. The region 'Armenian Highlands' already subtracted here covers only 147 of the principality's 183 cells, and the 661 shape put all 183 back, so the compiler gave the cells to the principality by the size rule at 658 and 661; the principality's own outline is now subtracted. Muslim conquest of Armenia page.

region.text: Medina and the Hejaz, the seat of the caliph

ledger.note: 632: Abu Bakr succeeds Muhammad at Medina as the first caliph. Infobox: 'Succession to Muhammad: 632'; 'Capital: Medina (632-656)'; 'Preceded by: First Islamic state'. The page gives Medina, not a boundary.

region.text: Arabia, in revolt after Muhammad's death

ledger.note: 632: the Ridda wars begin. 'The campaign against apostasy or the Ridda wars were fought and completed during the eleventh year of the Hijri.'

region.text: the Sawad, southern Iraq to the Tigris

ledger.note: 633: Khalid's Iraq campaign. 'Khalid's Iraq campaign began in 633'; the Persia page puts the conquest of Persia at 633-651.

region.text: the Arabian Peninsula, 'united under the caliph in Medina'

ledger.note: 633: Arabia is re-united. The peninsula was 'united under the caliph in Medina' by 12 AH, 'dawning on 18 March 633'.
633: the Ridda wars end with Arabia re-united (18 March 633).

region.text: Hira and the lower Euphrates, a few km from the later Kufa

ledger.note: 633: Khalid took Ullais 'in May' and 'attacked the city of Hira in the last week of the month' (infobox 'May 633'); 'The inhabitants paid a large tribute to spare the city', so Hira pays tribute rather than being annexed. Ubulla, Anbar and Ayn al-Tamr are not on this page; the next event keeps the wider southern Iraq at 634, confidence 1. The 100 km radius is below the resolution of the 633 shape.

region.text: Syria and Palestine, the first Arab raids

ledger.note: 634: the first campaigns into Syria and Palestine. Armies were dispatched in September 633 or spring 634; 'A Syriac chronicle places the first clash in February 634'; Bosra fell in May. The page gives no firm month for the first clash at Dathin and Badan near Gaza.

634: Damascus falls on 19 September 634 (Rashidun page); the Levant page says 'Damascus capitulated in sometime of August or September 635'. The two pages disagree by a year; 634 is the Rashidun page's, which also fits Cliopatria's 634 shape.

region.text: southern Iraq, the first conquests of Khalid

ledger.note: Year not on the pages for the wider southern Iraq: Hira is now its own event (May 633, Battle of Hira page), but the page is silent on Ubulla, Anbar and Ayn al-Tamr. Cliopatria's 634 shape contains about 40% of Mesopotamia, so 634 is my bridging.

region.text: the Ghassanid country on the Syrian frontier

ledger.note: 634: the Ghassanids. 'Khalid ibn al-Walid reached the Ghassanid Easter gathering at Marj Rahit on 24 April 634.' After Medina's appeals to the Ghassanids were rebuffed, the caliphate turned to the Kalb, Judham and Lakhm.

Year not on the page: the infobox lists the Ghassanids among the states preceding the caliphate and the Levant page is silent on their fate after the invasion (Jabala was their last king). 636 is the Yarmuk's year, my bridging. Re-checked on the Jabalah ibn al-Aiham page (2026-10-19): it gives no date for the transfer of the Ghassanid country; 'Jabala's flight to Byzantium supposedly occurred in c. 639' and his conversion to Islam is 'sometime after Yarmuk'. 636 stays a bridging.

Year not on the page: the contest with the Ghassanids ends when the whole of Syria falls after the Yarmuk (August 636, Rashidun page); the Levant page says nothing of the Ghassanids after the first campaign. The Jabalah ibn al-Aiham page (2026-10-19) is silent on an end date too: only Yarmuk (636) and his flight (c. 639).
636: the Yarmuk. 'Yarmouk (August 636) led to the whole of Syria falling into Muslim hands.' The Levant page gives no month or year for the battle.
637: Ctesiphon falls. Al-Qadisiyyah (636) opened the way and the capital 'fell in March 637' after a three-month siege; the Battle of Jalawla followed in April 637.
637: the fighting for the Sawad ends with Ctesiphon in March 637; by February 638 'the Suwad and the Tigris and Euphrates valleys were under full Muslim control'.
637: 'Jerusalem surrendered in April 637.'
637: 'Antioch surrendered on 30 October 637.' Aleppo and Qinnasrin fell 'in relatively quick succession' after the Yarmuk (Levant page, no dates).
637: the main war for Syria ends with Antioch (30 October 637); the coast of Palestine holds out to 639-641.

region.text: Khuzestan, where the Persian commander Hormuzan paid tribute

ledger.note: Late 638: Ahvaz. 'In late 638, a treaty made Hormuzan a tributary vassal. He later broke it.'

region.text: the Tigris and Euphrates valleys, Hulwan included

ledger.note: 638: Hulwan 'was captured in January 638' and 'By February 638, the Suwad and the Tigris and Euphrates valleys were under full Muslim control'. Tikrit and Mosul fell in the same period (undated).
638-639: 'Byzantine Armenia was conquered in 638-639' (Persia page). The Byzantine dossier of another group dates the loss 638.

region.text: Egypt, entered by Amr ibn al-As

ledger.note: 639: 'In December 639, Amr ibn al-As left for Egypt with a force of 4,000 troops.' Pelusium fell in February 640.

region.text: the Jazira (Upper Mesopotamia), conquered by Iyad ibn Ghanm

ledger.note: 639-640: 'In August 639 Iyad marched on Raqqa'; its capture is dated 639 or 640 and between late 639 and December 640 his forces 'subdued a series of cities'. Iyad died in 641.

region.text: the coast of Palestine: Caesarea and Ascalon

ledger.note: 639-641: 'Caesarea and Ascalon ... surrendered between 639 and 641'; 640 is the middle of the range.

region.text: Khuzestan, where Hormuzan broke his treaty

ledger.note: Year not on the page: Hormuzan 'later broke' the late-638 treaty; 'Persian reinforcements arrived in late 640', so 640 is my bridging. Re-checked on the Hormuzan page (2026-10-19): both breaches of tribute are undated ('he soon stopped paying tribute'; 'he later stopped paying tribute'), he fled to Shushtar 'sometime later in 641' and was taken 'in 642' (lead) or 641 (body). 640 stays a bridging.
Late 640: Persian reinforcements arrive and the Battle of Tustar follows (the page gives no month for Tustar).

region.text: Khuzestan, with Susa and Junde Sabur

ledger.note: 641: Susa was 'captured in January 641 after a siege of a couple of months'; Junde Sabur surrendered after a siege of a few weeks (undated).
641: the Khuzestan campaign ends with Susa in January 641.

region.text: Lower Nubia, the Christian kingdom of Nubia

ledger.note: 642: 'In the summer of 642, 'Amr ibn al-'As sent an expedition to the Christian kingdom of Nubia.' The Rashidun page says Umar's 642 campaign failed. The Cliopatria seed lists Nobatia (641-655) as the neighbour; the page says only 'Nubia'.

region.text: Derbent and the Caspian gate up to Balanjar

ledger.note: 642: 'The first Arab invasion began in 642 with the capture of the strategically important city of Derbent.'

642: Egypt is Muslim. The infobox runs 'December 639-September 642'; 'the 11 months of armistice ended' on 29 September (642). The Rashidun page has a treaty for Alexandria 'signed on 8 November 641' and Egypt 'conquered by 642'; the Egypt page has Cyrus of Alexandria's treaty on 22 December and the first tribute on 10 December 641.
642: the Egyptian campaign ends with the end of the armistice on 29 September.

region.text: the Median plateau: Nahavand and Hamadan

ledger.note: 642: the Persians were defeated 'at the Battle of Nahavand in December 642'; the Hamadan district fell after it with weak resistance (it rebelled and was retaken in 651).

Year not on the page: the page never dates Rey's first submission, but says 'Hamadan and Rey had rebelled' and, in the Khorasan paragraph, 'Rey was already in Muslim hands', so Rey was under Muslim authority before 651. The sasanian-empire dossier hands Media over in 642 (its /ledger/114); 642 is my bridging, in step with the Hamadan event of December 642.

region.text: Isfahan, taken after al-Nu'man's campaign from Hamadan

ledger.note: Year not on the page: Isfahan was taken after Nahavand and the siege lasted 'a few months', with conflicting commander accounts and no surrender date. 643 is my bridging. Re-checked on the Isfahan page (2026-10-19): it says 'When the Arabs captured Isfahan in 642 CE' and names no commander; the Persia page puts Nahavand in December 642 and a siege of a few months after it, and the sasanian-empire dossier has 643. 643 is kept; the one-year disagreement between the pages is not resolved.

region.text: Kerman, subdued by Suhail ibn Adi

ledger.note: 643: 'Suhail ibn Adi marched from Basra in 643 and subdued the province after a pitched battle.'

642/643: 'Soon after the fall of Alexandria in 642, Amr ibn al-As continued westwards into Cyrenaica and Tripolitania'; 'Barqa fell without opposition, treaties were made with the Luwata Berbers exacting a tribute of 13,000 dinars'. The page gives no year for Barqa itself, so 643 is the page's date for Tripoli carried back to the same campaign; the byzantine-empire dossier has the loss in 644 (643-644). Moved from 647 (the Rashidun page's Sufetula year, which does not date either).
643: 'Tripoli was more difficult, its garrison being supported by the Christian Berber tribes of Nafusa, but after around a month it also fell in around 643.' Moved from 647.

region.text: the South Caucasus, 'almost the whole' of it, and Iranian Azerbaijan

ledger.note: 644: expeditions reached Tiflis in late 643 and 'By Umar's death in November 644, almost the whole of the South Caucasus' was captured. The Rashidun page lists Azerbaijan, Dagestan, Armenia and Georgia, 'later re-conquered during Uthman's reign'. Atropatene is added here: the Persia page has 'Azerbaijan then surrendered to Caliph Umar, agreeing to pay the annual jizya' (undated, so by November 644), which is why the 646 revolt below can end in a reconquest. The Muslim conquest of Armenia page (opened 2026-10-19) has only raids in 639/640, 642 and 645 before 653, against the Persia page's 'Byzantine Armenia was conquered in 638-639' and 'almost the whole of the South Caucasus'; the disagreement is kept, the Persia page used.

region.text: Makran, the coast of Gedrosia up to the Indus frontier

ledger.note: 644: 'In late 644 CE Caliph Umar dispatched an army under the command of Hakam ibn Amr for the wholesale invasion of Makran' (a raid in 643); 'In mid-644 the Battle of Rasil was fought' against the Rai dynasty, and Umar ordered that Makran 'should be the easternmost frontier'. The page names no ruler of Makran before the King of Rai's army, and no Rai dynasty dossier exists, so the counterpart is nobody. The 644 keyframe keeps only Makran of the Pakistani land Cliopatria draws.

End of 645: 'Constans sent a large fleet of 300 ships to retake Egypt towards the end of 645'; Manuel's troops 'landed without resistance and easily overpowered small Arab garrison at Alexandria' (about 1000 Arab soldiers).

646: 'The main rebellions were in the Persian provinces of Armenia and Azerbaijan in 646' (Persia page). Re-typed from a loss to kingdom-of-armenia (review of 2026-10-19): the Armenian rebels were the princes under Theodore Rshtuni, whom the Muslim conquest of Armenia page has recognised by Constans II and then 'Byzantine suzerainty', not the Cliopatria Kingdom of Armenia. The land stays in the shape while contested.

646: Amr, sent by Uthman, beat the Byzantines at the Battle of Nikiou, who 'retreated in disarray, back to Alexandria'; 'the Arabs managed to batter the walls down and storm the city'. The body gives no year for the storming; 646 is the infobox's '645-646' and the byzantine-empire dossier's /ledger/15.
646: the same sentence names Azerbaijan; 'The conquest of Iranian Azerbaijan started in 651', so the revolt runs to 651. The Atropatene rebels were not the Armenian kingdom.

region.text: southern Tunisia around Sufetula, raided from Cyrenaica

ledger.note: 647: Sufetula. The army 'assembled in Cyrenaica, took Tripoli, and defeated the Exarchate at Sufetula in 647'.

Year not on the page: 'Muslim forces later withdrew to Barqa'. The Exarchate dossier of another group dates the tribute and the end to 648; the raid took no ground. Re-checked on the Battle of Sufetula (647) page (2026-10-19): the battle is 647 ('took place in 647'); 'the Arabs agreed to depart in exchange for the payment of a heavy tribute in gold', with no year and no destination for the withdrawal. 648 stays a bridging.

648: 'Istakhr surrendered in 648.' Fars had been raided since 638/9; Bishapur made peace c. 643, rebelled and was beaten in 646; Istakhr rebelled in 649/650 and was sacked, with Gor, Kazerun and Siraf seized in 650/651.

649: 'Mu'awiya's navy took Cyprus in 649, and Crete and Rhodes followed.' The Rashidun page says 'In 650, Mu'awiya attacked Cyprus' and the Arab-Byzantine wars page (opened for the Umayyad dossier) 'Cyprus and Crete were captured in 653'.
649: the rebellions list has 'Fars and Sistan in 649'; Istakhr's citizens 'rebelled in 649/650'. Bishapur had also declared independence in 646 (al-Baladhuri), not drawn.

region.text: Hamadan and Rey, which rebelled and were retaken

ledger.note: Year not on the page: 'Meanwhile, Hamadan and Rey had rebelled' is undated and sits in the 651 paragraph, so 650 is my bridging; the reconquest is 651. This replaces the 651 gain of Rey from the Sasanians, which the 642 loss of Media on their side contradicted.

region.text: Makran, the coast of Gedrosia up to the Indus frontier

ledger.note: 650: the rebellions list reads 'Fars and Sistan in 649, Makran in 650, and Khorasan in 651'.

651: 'Ahnaf ibn Qais took Nishapur without resistance', Herat fell after a siege of a few months and Merv was 'occupied without a fight'; Yazdegerd III was killed near Merv in 651. The Transoxiana page: 'Marw, the capital of Khorasan, fell in 651', bringing the border to the Oxus.
651: 'Rabi ibn Ziyad took Zaranj, and its governor Aparviz agreed to a tribute of 1 million dirhams'; Sistan had rebelled in 649 and Mujashi's 650 invasion was beaten.

region.text: Hamadan and Rey, which rebelled and were retaken

ledger.note: 651: 'Nu'aym recaptured Hamadan after a bloody battle, and then proceeded to Rey'; Rey was 'besieged' and 'surrendered after fierce resistance', the Persians 'were defeated outside the fort, and the Muslims recaptured the city'. Re-typed from a gain from the Sasanians (review of 2026-10-19): the land was Muslim from 642.

region.text: Azerbaijan: Zanjan, Ardabil and Bab al-Abwab

ledger.note: 651: the Azerbaijan reconquest 'started in 651' (Hudhayfah took Zanjan, Ardabil 'which surrendered peacefully' and Bab al-Abwab 'by force'); the page also has Azerbaijan surrendering to Umar, who died in 644, which it does not reconcile. Counterpart changed from the Sasanians to the rebels (review of 2026-10-19).

650/651: Istakhr 'was soon sacked by the Arabs, who killed over 40,000 defenders' and they 'quickly seized Gor, Kazerun and Siraf'; 'Muslim control of Fars remained shaky for a time, with several local rebellions following'. The page gives 650/651; 651 is used.

region.text: Makran, the coast of Gedrosia up to the Indus frontier

ledger.note: Outcome not on the page: Makran is only named in 651 as 'part of a simultaneous attack launched against Kerman and Makran in the southeast'. Ending the revolt in 651 is my bridging.
651: Hudhayfah's march ends the Azerbaijani revolt that began in 646.

region.text: Derbent and the Caspian gate up to Balanjar

ledger.note: 652: Balanjar. The first Arab-Khazar war ended there with 'a decisive defeat' of the Arabs in 652 and the death of Abd al-Rahman ibn Rabi'a.
651-2: 'A treaty was finally concluded with the Nubians in 651-2'; the Rashidun page calls it a non-aggression treaty after Uthman's governor sent another army 'ten years later'.
653: 'Rshtuni voluntarily agreed to submit to Muslim overlordship' when Constans' truce with the Arabs ended in 653; the page gives no 652/653 treaty date beyond that.

653: Armenia submits under Rshtuni and stays a tributary; the page has Rshtuni evicting Byzantine garrisons in 654 and invaded Byzantine Armenia in 655; he died at Damascus in 656. Drawn as a vassal, outside the shape from 653.
656: the capital moves from Medina to Kufa (infobox: 'Medina (632-656); Kufa (656-661)'). The First Fitna page has Ali going to Kufa to gather troops; it does not call it a capital.

region.text: Syria, held by Mu'awiya, with Cyprus, which his fleet had taken

ledger.note: 656: Uthman is killed 'in June 656' and Ali's accession 'triggered the First Fitna'; Mu'awiya, long governor of the Levant, holds Syria against Ali (the Rashidun page: Ali's forces 'lost control over most of the caliphate's territory to Mu'awiya'). Cyprus (gained 649) goes with Syria: the umayyad-caliphate 656 keyframe includes it, and this keyframe drops it.

region.text: Basra, seized by Talha's and al-Zubayr's party

ledger.note: Dec 656: 'Rebels captured Basra from Ali's governor'; 'The two parties fought the Battle of the Camel in December 656' and Ali won; fighting there began on 8 December.
Dec 656: Ali wins the Battle of the Camel and holds Basra.

657: 'with the outbreak of the First Muslim Civil War in 657, effective Arab authority in the country ceased'; Mamikonian 'returned to Byzantine overlordship almost immediately'. Mu'awiya made the princes re-submit in 661 (Umayyad dossier).
657: the Armenian princes return to Byzantine overlordship (mirror of byzantine-empire /ledger/20, which cites the same page).

region.text: the front between Ali's Iraq and Mu'awiya's Syria, where the armies met at Siffin

ledger.note: 657: Siffin. 'Fighting began on Wednesday, 26 July' and an arbitration agreement followed on 2 August 657; a stalemate. The page I read does not place the battlefield.

658: 'In mid-658, Mu'awiya I intervened directly in Egypt'; Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr (who replaced Qays ibn Sa'd in 657) was executed and Amr ibn al-As reinstated: 'the Umayyad annexation of Egypt took place in 658'.

region.text: the Hejaz and Yemen, entered by Mu'awiya's general Busr

ledger.note: 660: 'In 660, Busr then continued his expedition into Yemen'; Ali held the Hejaz and Yemen until Busr's raids, and Jariya later restored his authority in Yemen.

region.text: the front between Ali's Iraq and Mu'awiya's Syria

ledger.note: Late 660: letters between Ali and Mu'awiya: 'both parties agreed to cease military campaigns'; the offer that Ali keep Iraq and Mu'awiya Syria.
661: Hasan cedes the caliphate and the contest ends.

region.text: the rest of the caliphate: Arabia, Iraq and Iran

ledger.note: 661: 'In January 661, while praying at the Great Mosque of Kufa', Ali was killed; Hasan, proclaimed at Kufa, 'concluded a peace treaty with Mu'awiya', ceding the caliphate after six months. Mu'awiya 'received formal oaths of allegiance in Jerusalem' (Rashidun page).

region.text: the Rashidun Caliphate at Hasan's abdication

ledger.note: 661: the Rashidun Caliphate ends. Infobox: 'Hasan-Mu'awiya treaty and establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate: 661'; Hasan 'briefly assumed the caliphate for six months before reaching an agreement to abdicate'. Cliopatria continues the Name to 665.

wars.name: Ridda wars

zones.text: the apostate tribes of the peninsula

wars.outcome: Medina's victory: the peninsula 'united under the caliph in Medina' by 18 March 633.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Persia
wars.outcome: Muslim victory: 'Annexation of the Sasanian Empire by the Rashidun Caliphate'; Yazdegerd III killed near Merv in 651. The infobox of the Persia page reads 633-651; the Rashidun page's infobox has 633-654.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of the Levant
wars.outcome: Muslim victory: 'Annexation of Byzantine Syria by the Rashidun Caliphate' (infobox 634-638); Damascus 634/5, Yarmuk August 636, Jerusalem April 637, Antioch October 637.
wars.note: The Levant page dates the infobox 634-638 but the Jazira and the coast fall in 639-641.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Muslim victory: Egypt 'under Arab rule within two years'; the Byzantines briefly retook Alexandria at the end of 645 and Amr retook it in 646.

wars.name: Arab-Khazar wars (first war)
wars.outcome: Khazar victory at Balanjar in 652: the first Arab invasion began in 642 with Derbent and ended in a decisive Arab defeat.
wars.note: The second war (722-737) is in the Umayyad dossier.

wars.name: First Fitna
wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: Ali killed January 661, Hasan abdicated, 'Establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate'.

certainty.note: Desert and steppe frontiers and conquest-era control; no treaty line. Egypt, the Sawad and Syria are firmer once garrison cities exist (Fustat, Kufa, Basra) but no page draws a boundary.

notes:
Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19. Pages: the Rashidun Caliphate article, the Persia, Levant and Egypt conquests and the First Fitna (five, the budget), plus the Arab-Khazar wars page reused from the Umayyad dossier for 642-652. Dates are as WebFetch returned them.
Page disagreements kept in the notes: Damascus 19 September 634 (Rashidun page) against August/September 635 (Levant page); Cyprus 649 (Levant), 650 (Rashidun) and 653 (Arab-Byzantine wars); Tripoli c. 643 (Maghreb page) against 647 (Rashidun page); Persia 633-651 (Persia infobox) against 633-654 (Rashidun infobox); the Egypt page's Babylon dates (20 December / 6 April 641) are unreconciled.
Cliopatria problems: the 661-665 shape continues the Rashidun name after Ali's death (verdict adjust, 661 only); 644-650 gives Khorasan, Sistan and Afghanistan before 651; the shape lacks Cyprus, Khuzestan before 644 and Egypt is kept in 658-660. The Muslim state of Muhammad (622-632) is a separate dossier. Not on the pages opened: the dates of Hira and the first Iraqi towns (634 gain at confidence 1), the Kabul valley and Tokharistan fighting (the Tokhara dossier dates it 652-653), Makran, Crete and Rhodes, Armenian princes' status after 646, the Hejaz-Yemen governors.
Tabaristan: the Persia page dates a peace treaty of 'the ruler of Tabaristan' to 651 but says nothing of tribute and does not name him; the Dabuyid dossier carries the relation and no vassal event is recorded here.
Counterparts without a dossier of their own: Ridda rebels, Hormuzan (Ahvaz), Talha and al-Zubayr (Basra rebels). Gazetteer: 'Ascalon' (Ashkelon) is not a place name there; a 30 km radius around 34.57 E, 31.66 N stands in for it.
Repair of 2026-10-19 (review me-07): the predecessor land is the Hejaz (applied by the reviewer). Armenia and Azerbaijan: the 646 'loss' to kingdom-of-armenia is now two contest pairs with the rebels (Atropatene 646-651; the Armenian princes under Theodore Rshtuni 646-653), Armenia a tributary 653-657 and a loss to byzantine-empire in 657 (Muslim conquest of Armenia page); Atropatene is gained in 644 with Transcaucasia. Fars is held back until 648 and has a revolt pair 649-651; Rey and Hamadan are a reconquest of 651 (rebels), not a gain from the Sasanians. Makran is gained in 644 (Makran page) and has a revolt pair 650-651; the Pakistani land outside Makran is taken out of the keyframes. Cyrenaica and Tripolitania move from 647 to 643 (Maghreb page) and are added to the keyframes from 643. Alexandria is lost at the end of 645 and retaken in 646 (Egypt page). Cyprus goes with Syria in 656. Thin items re-read: Hira is 633 (Battle of Hira page); the Ghassanid, Hormuzan, Isfahan and Sufetula pages are silent or differ by a year and the events stay at confidence 1. Open: Afghanistan beyond Khorasan and Sistan stays in the 651-660 shapes with no gain event; Tabaristan is not taken out of the 651-660 shapes although the Dabuyids hold it; Georgia and Caucasian Albania stay in the shapes from 644 although the Umayyad dossier gains them in 705; which side held Libya in 658-660 is not on any page.
